messages:
emma_support: FYI ACME reported 503s to their private API svc-internal.acme.internal after a recent VPC peering change. They see intermittent NXDOMAIN when hitting our private endpoint path. I have their dig + curl snippets.

infra-bot: :rotating_light: Alert: private-api 503 in us-west-2 at 2026-03-17T10:23:00Z. Incident INC-2029

mike-sre: Can you paste the dig output from inside their VPC and one from our VPC? Also traceroute to our egress/resolver IPs.

emma_support: From their engineer (copied):
```
$ dig svc-internal.acme.internal @172.31.0.2 +short
; <<>> DiG 9.11.3 <<>> svc-internal.acme.internal @172.31.0.2 +short
;; ->>HEADER<<- opcode: QUERY, status: NXDOMAIN, id: 12345
```
They also curl'd our internal ELB and got HTTP/1.1 503.

raj_eng: Sounds like split-horizon / private hosted zone overlap. We should check Route53 hosted zones & VPC associations for acme.internal across accounts.

lina-netops: Quick audit shows two private hosted zones with identical names:
- Z1 (acme-prod) associated with vpc-aaaa (ACME account)
- Z2 (redwood-prod) associated with vpc-bbbb (our account)
Z2 appears to have only NS/SOA and no A records for svc-internal.

mike-sre: That explains NXDOMAIN: if a private hosted zone exists in the resolver path with no record, Route53 returns NXDOMAIN even if another account's zone has the record. Behavior depends on which zone/VPC association the resolver hits.

emma_support: Timeline: customer removed a cross-account assoc and re-associated a different VPC ~10:15PT. Reports started ~10:23PT.

raj_eng: Repro steps for us:
1) From acme VPC host: dig svc-internal.acme.internal @<acme-resolver-ip>
2) From our VPC host: dig svc-internal.acme.internal @<our-resolver-ip>
3) Check SOA to see which zone is answering: dig +noall +answer soa svc-internal.acme.internal

emma_support: From our tester (redwood VPC):
```
$ dig svc-internal.acme.internal @172.31.0.2 soa +noall +answer
svc-internal.acme.internal. 300 IN SOA ns-23.awsdns-02.com. hostmaster.acme.internal. 1 7200 900 1209600 300
```
SOA points to the acme account, but peered queries sometimes hit Z2 which has no records.

lina-netops: Hypothesis: overlapping private zone owned by us (Z2) is shadowing the acme zone for some peered paths. Options:
- Remove/disassociate Z2 from vpc-bbbb if unused (preferred).
- Add missing records or alias to Z2 (bad long-term).
- Configure Route53 Resolver rule forwarding to acme's resolver inbound endpoint.

mike-sre: Note: if choosing resolver-forwarding, ensure outbound resolver IPs are allowed in customer's firewall/egress allowlist.

raj_eng: Customer impact list: internal-auditor, batch jobs. NXDOMAIN TTLs may cause client caching—expect some residual errors until TTL expiry.

emma_support: Customer approved disassociation during a maintenance window. Scheduling for 02:00 UTC.

infra-bot: Job queued: route53-vpc-change R53JOB-789. Patch window 02:00-02:10 UTC.

mike-sre: Post-change checks:
```
# from acme host
dig svc-internal.acme.internal @172.31.0.2 +short
# expect an A record instead of NXDOMAIN
```
Allow for ~60s resolver cache TTL before attempting retries.

emma_support: Update 02:05 UTC — disassociation completed, customer confirms 200 responses and no more NXDOMAIN. Closing incident.

lina-netops: Follow-up: we'll remove Z2 if unused and document no-overlap policy for private hosted zones to avoid future split-horizon collisions.

mike-sre: Also add a preflight checklist for VPC peering changes: list private hosted zones with same name across accounts and flag overlap.

emma_support: Thanks team :thumbsup: Closing thread.
